b

you mean both LLDP Tx & Rx enabled for all interfaces?
how do we control LLDP enable/disable for specific interface?
why do we need interface to enable LLDP on all interfaces at once?

This is for the case where the user wants to deactivate LLDP operation entirely. 
For enable/disable for specific interface, we can add this property to TLVs.interface.yaml.
I dont think “Per interface Enable/Disable LLDP” property under the TLVs interface would be correct.

We have the LLDPEnabled Property defined in Port schema that is "per" interface.
```
        LLDPEnabled:
          description: Enable/disable LLDP for this port.
          readOnly: false
          type: boolean
          x-longDescription: This property shall contain the state indicating whether
            to enable LLDP for a port.  If LLDP is disabled at the adapter level,
            this property shall be ignored.
```

There is no redfish property that can be set by the user to entirely enable/disable LLDP. So, I would suggest we use this same interface for enabling lldp, but implement it under each interface.

Like, /xyz/openbmc_project/network/lldp/eth[01] can implement xyz.openbmc_project.Network.LLDP.Settings.

xyz.openbmc_project.Network.EthernetInterface has the EmitLLDP property that enables/disables LLDP entirely. So the consideration was to maintain the same capability, but in a separate LLDP interface.
I added enable/disable LLDP to TLVs.interface.yaml

Yes, but that's for each ethernet interface.
https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-networkd/commit/f7116de80882b7edad729e7d8747639eff600b08

That's the reason i suggested if we can have this interface implemented by each Ethernet interface dbus object
I will update the wording in Settings.interface.yaml, to Enables or disables LLDP packet transmission for a specific interface.
Done
Done

its possible to have multiple Management Addresses published in lldp 
how to handle multiple ip addresses?

We would need to change it to array type. Is there a use case for that?
The interface here follows the DMTF scheme that supports only one Management Addresses for IPv4 and one for IPv6.

It is possible for one interface to advertise IP on all ethernet interfaces by configuring it in lldpd.conf

https://redfishforum.com/thread/1216/request-change-managementaddressipv-types-arrays?page=1&scrollTo=4691
started this thread to discuss on the same.

Sure, it is possible to advertise multiply IP addresses in one interface. I can change the specification. 
However, if Redfish rejects the change request, it is probably best to keep it like it is now.
Done

I dont think adding this property under TLVs interface is appropriate. 

Two suggestions here:
1. Since in this interface's description you have mentioned as "Includes TLVs", renaming this interface to something like "*.Network.LLDP.Properties" might help.

-- or --

2. Have this property in a new interface that can be implemented under each ethernet object.
I think the renaming the interface is better than creating an additional interface.

Actually, to be fully Complient to Redfish we need enable/disable per interface.
Putting with a the TLV, we will have separate enable/disable for the receive and transmit object, and Redfish doesn't support that.
Correct. So what we have now in redfish is `per interface "enable/disable"`. Then the transmit and receive object's properties may be populated based on this "enabled" value.
Does enabling LLDP on an interface automatically turn on both receive and transmit by default? Is there a way to enable only one of them?

Abhilash, in Redfish LLDPEnabled property is separated from the transmit and receive properties, it turns on both. While in the DBus service we can add separate EnableLLDP properties to transmit and receive, and it will work, we won't be able to access these properties from Redfish.
So at least for first version of the service, I think we should keep it Redfish compliant.
Done

@ugoldfeld@nvidia.com
If you are planning to change the name of the TLVs interface, can we also add a "Status" property?

Reason behind asking this is:
Say, lldpd stops receiving packets on an interface, then this property might indicate the state of the neighbor. Something like: https://github.com/ibm-openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/1120/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Network/Neighbor.interface.yaml#L28

I stand corrected here, "Status" should not be given under this interface, because it should be in the interface level (meaning, if there are no lldp packets on eth0, then eth0 lldp status should be updated). Also, Settings interface should be in ethernet interface level (enable/disable lldp).

Tx/Rx objects of each ethernet interface should implement the TLVs interface.

I there are no  lldp packets on eth0, periodic refresh of LLDP dbus objects makes sure the receive object of eth0 doesn't exist. So what is the use case of the "status" property? 
I updated the wording so that settings interface is in ethernet interface level

D-bus interfaces looks good.
I believe changes needed in ManagementAddressIPv4 & ManagementAddressIPv6 property type once redfish accepts schema changes, these changes can be done in next commit.
